superseded.prompt:
Production sprite atlas for the approved A / COLLAR FOLD paired-throw animation. EXACTLY SIX full-body sprites of the SAME SINGLE CHARACTER on a fully transparent background, arranged in a roomy equal THREE-COLUMN by TWO-ROW grid. Landscape 1536x1024 canvas. All cells have generous transparent gutters, all boots, fingers, hair, garments and entire weapons must fit their own cell. No labels, lettering, arrows, frames, ground, shadows, other people, sparks, smears, blur or translucent ghost limbs. These are individual isolated sprite drawings that will be composited into a two-fighter hold in game.

IDENTITY: ANVIL: very stocky short broad dwarf, bald, huge braided white beard, orange arm tattoos, black-and-bronze heavy smith armour, red sash, heavy brown boots. Right hand keeps his short forging hammer; left forearm bears his tall rectangular anvil-emblem shield. He captures with the leading shield/forearm rim braced across the opponent's collar, never by dropping his equipment. Use the attached current character sheet as exact face, costume, anatomy, weapon and crisp cel-shading authority. Same anatomy scale, head size and boot size in ALL six cells; bending must not enlarge the character. Preserve strong mature fighting-game proportions, crisp ink and two/three-tone graphic shadows. Feet consistently grounded on an invisible baseline within each row. Every pose is based on a three-quarter RIGHT-facing game camera.

TOP ROW = character is the GRABBER. Three distinct expressive pose keys:
Top left CATCH: wide planted stance, forward arm/forearm reaches to screen-right at upper-chest height, elbow slightly bent, gripping point beyond front shoulder. Rear weapon/hand stays controlled. Fierce focused expression.
Top middle LOAD/HOLD: maintain that same forward collar contact, hips lower and pull back, elbow folds toward the chest and down, chest/shoulder pressure loads a compact collar fold. Strong readable anticipation, visibly different from catch, no whole-body size change. Forward contact point is at middle chest height.
Top right TURN/FINISH LOAD: braced planted foot pivots, hips rotate left and rear shoulder is slightly more visible; still holding the opponent in the forward forearm at chest height. Loaded diagonal pull, poised for a sudden release. This is a compact controlled quarter-turn, NOT a flying throw, not a new attack.

BOTTOM ROW = character is the CAPTURED RECEIVER, facing screen-right toward an invisible opponent on the RIGHT. Do NOT draw that opponent or their hands.
Bottom left CAUGHT: collar/upper chest pulled forward while chin and shoulders recoil slightly up/back, knees soften; front collar area clear for the other fighter's grip. Arms and weapons tense low/outside the torso rather than calmly resting. Clearly trapped, off balance.
Bottom middle COLLAR FOLD: sternum and shoulders fold toward screen-right, knees flex, hips resist backward left, head lowered and expression strained; compact powerful bend, not a deep bow. Keep visible front collar where external hand can contact. Arms/weapon remain outside contact area. This is the approved forward-compression direction.
Bottom right TURNED FOLD: same compressed hold, hips and torso pivot to a three-quarter rear/right view with far shoulder more visible, one heel rotates; retain compact silhouette and same body scale, for a backward throw transition. No airborne pose.

Largest changes are the catch to compression and final torso rotation, not cosmetic flutter. Keep costume landmarks and handedness absolutely consistent. Exactly six isolated full-body drawings, no extra characters, no opponents, true alpha transparency.
